book.rats.name: book.rats.start.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes: You start with six rats, each with a random standard coat and one inherited strength. Breed them to mix coats and traits. Parents with only plain coat alleles have a 1 in 32 chance per pup of a new standard coat.\n\nOn the RATS + CARE shelf at Quayside Canning Co-op, single rats renew weekly: standard coats (60 credits) from day 7; hairless (90), heavy and milk lines (100) from day 14; rare coats (180) from day 21.

book.rats.name: book.rats.traits.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes:
The animal tooltip names inherited strengths and weaknesses. Level I is at least 20% above the species baseline, II at least 50%. Thrifty eater is the reverse: 20% or 35% less hunger.

Breeder: fertility. Large litters: litter size. Meaty: growth and weight. Long-lived: old-age threshold. Hardy: immunity. Sturdy: maximum health. Thrifty eater: hunger.

Labels add no bonus of their own. Either sex passes any trait, males included.

book.rats.name: book.rats.selection.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes:
Each pup takes one allele per stat from each parent, with the usual mutations; better is never guaranteed. Each starter line has its own bent:

Charcoal/Smoke: fertility, litter size; eats more. Slate/Blue-grey: fast growth; eats more. Chestnut/Fawn: long life; slower growth. Russet/Cinnamon: immunity, health; less fertile. Olive agouti/Cream: eats less; slower growth.

Cross lines to combine strengths, and mark keepers with the marking pen.

book.rats.name: book.rats.coats.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes: Five standard coats, each with a male and a female shade: Charcoal/Smoke, Slate/Blue-grey, Chestnut/Fawn, Russet/Cinnamon, Olive agouti/Cream.\n\nEach pup gets one coat allele from each parent. Of two different standard coats, the earlier in this list shows and the other is carried. Coats do not change fertility or health. Colour alone never reveals carried alleles: keep records.

book.rats.name: book.rats.rare.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes: Pearl, Champagne and Silver are rare coats, in either sex. A rare coat shows only when both alleles match; crossed with any other coat, it leaves unseen carriers. Two carriers of the same rare coat give about one rare pup in four.\n\nExtra furry is a separate recessive trait needing both fur alleles. Russet/Cinnamon starters carry two: cross them into any coat.

book.rats.name: book.rats.market.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes: Care and weight still set meat yield. Live rats also have a pet value: standard coats add 15%, rare coats 100%, shaggy fur 15%, cow spots 30%. Markings and breeding traits add more.\n\nRats and fish share 40 breeding traits. Young take after either parent or develop a new one; seven on one offspring is a 1 in 10,000 birth. Some regulars, and about one household visitor in five, ask for a pet at the counter.

book.rats.name: book.rats.markings.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes:
Traits show on the rat itself, in every coat and growth stage.

Meaty: fuller back and body. Sturdy: broader shoulder. Extra furry: rough, tufted outline.

Breeder: pale flank saddle. Large litters: pale belly. Long-lived: pale muzzle. Hardy: dark back stripe. Thrifty eater: pale rump.

Markings show expressed traits only, never carriers, pregnancy or disease.

book.rats.name: book.rats.hairless.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes: Hairless is a second recessive coat-texture form: two hairless alleles give bare skin, one is carried unseen. Extra furry x hairless gives smooth carriers of both.\n\nA Meaty II rat grows a very heavy body once it reaches 180 g, and loses it if starvation drops it below. Heavy stock grows fast and eats more, but starts at newborn weight. Neither form adds a price bonus.

book.rats.name: book.rats.milk.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes:
Cow spots mark an inherited milk line. Two milk-line alleles show spots; one is carried unseen. Males pass it on but give no milk.

After a litter, an adult spotted female gives up to 10 mL of milk a day for seven fed days. Select her, then target an owned bottle or jug with at least 1 mL free. Uncollected milk is lost at day's end.

Keep her fed and clean: hunger stops the milk, and illness contaminates it.

book.rats.name: book.fish.tank.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes: These lines cover all six native species: tilapia, gutter tilapia, graft tilapia, eel, electric eel and sturgeon. Tank, food and harvest rules are unchanged; bought juveniles still need raising.\n\nOn the FISH + CARE shelf, click NEXT SPECIES to cycle through them. Standard colours arrive on day 14, rare ones on day 28, one fish per weekly offer. Eels and sturgeon now breed in a stocked tank. Male sturgeon are sold here too; only females give caviar.

book.rats.name: book.fish.appearance.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes: Tilapia have five standard colours, each with a male and a female shade: Bronze/Copper, Moss/Olive, Cobalt/Blue-grey, Charcoal/Smoke, Red/Coral. Pearl, Gold and Platinum are rare. Eels and sturgeon have their own five standard and three rare colours.\n\nColour, fin colour and pattern are three separate gene pairs. Fins, patterns and rare colours show only when both alleles match; a mixed pair is carried unseen. The tooltip names what a fish shows.

book.rats.name: book.fish.breeding.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes:
An eel clutch is 3 fry (5% laying chance; electric eel 4%), a sturgeon clutch 2 (3%). Fry need 3 fed days (eel) or 4 (sturgeon) to grow.

A fed adult male of the same species fathers the clutch; with several, one is chosen at random, so keep one pair to control parentage.

Each fry gets one allele per gene from each parent. Parents with only ordinary colours have a 1 in 32 chance per fry of a new common colour.

book.rats.name: book.fish.traits.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes:
Four gene pairs change the native numbers. Two selected alleles give the full effect, mixed pairs less.

Meaty: up to 20% faster growth when fed; calorie costs stay.
Long-lived: old-age threshold up to 30% later.
Thrifty: up to 20% less maintenance energy; growth costs stay.
Breeder: up to 40% higher laying chance, capped at 100%; no extra roll or larger clutch.

Faster growth also advances the biological-age clock: pair Meaty with Long-lived.

book.rats.name: book.fish.value.body
Rat Keeper's Breeding Notes: Live fish have a pet value: standard colours add 15%, rare colours 100%, most patterns 10%, the two rare eel and sturgeon patterns 40% or 60%. Breeding traits add more.\n\nRats and fish share 40 breeding traits. Young take after either parent or develop a new one; seven on one offspring is a 1 in 10,000 birth. Some regulars, and about one household visitor in five, ask for a pet at the counter.
